# Reproduction Results

This document demonstrates the reproduction of key results from the paper "Channelling Multimodality Through a Unimodalizing Transport: Warp-U Sampler and Stochastic Bridge Sampling Estimator".

## Figure 6: Radial Velocity Signal and Marginal Posterior Distribution

```{r fig6, fig.width=12, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Time series of radial velocity (RV) data and density estimation of mean anomaly.", fig.pos="H"}
# Libraries
library(mvtnorm)
library(mnormt)
library(numDeriv)
library(stats4)
library(MASS)
library(bayestestR)
library(numbers)
library(ggpubr)

# Load data
load('../data/dataset1_one_planet_posterior.RData')
load('../data/prior_bounds.RData')
load('../data/stanData.RData')

# Process RV data
results_sample = list()
results_sample$w_all = data
P_data = results_sample$w_all[,2]

period_est = map_estimate(P_data)$MAP_Estimate
period_adjusted = (data_now$time %% period_est)/period_est

# Get other parameter estimates
K_est = map_estimate(results_sample$w_all[,3])$MAP_Estimate
e_est = map_estimate(results_sample$w_all[,4])$MAP_Estimate
w_est = map_estimate(results_sample$w_all[,5])$MAP_Estimate
M0_est = map_estimate(results_sample$w_all[,6])$MAP_Estimate
planet_paras <- list()
planet_paras[[1]] <- list(tau=period_est,K=K_est,e=e_est,w=w_est,M0=M0_est,gamma=0)

# Prepare data for plotting
time_dense = seq(from = 0, to = 600, length.out = 1000)
RV_get_dense = v(time_dense,planet_paras[[1]])
phrase_dense = (time_dense %% period_est)/period_est
RV_data_dense = data.frame(time_dense, phrase_dense, RV_get_dense)

# Create RV_data_plot first
RV_data_plot = data.frame(data_now, period_adjusted = period_adjusted)
RV_data_plot$RV_getfrom_function = v(RV_data_plot$time, planet_paras[[1]])

# Plot 1: RV time series
p1_plot = ggplot(RV_data_plot, aes(time, rv)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = 'RV'), shape = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = time, y = rv, ymin = rv-sd, ymax = rv+sd, color = 'RV'),
                alpha = I(3/7), width = .03, position = position_dodge(0.05)) +
  geom_line(data = RV_data_dense, 
            aes(time_dense, RV_get_dense, color = 'predicted radial velocity at time t'),
            size = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  ylab("RV (m/s)") +
  xlab('Time') +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.position = 'none',
        legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue"))

# Load data for density estimation
load('../data/PL_samples_Real_plot.RData')  # PT data
# Process PT data
sample_results = t(PL_list[[1]][ 1 , ,])
PT_sample_results = sample_results#results_sample$w_all
variable_num = 6
PT_density = density(PT_sample_results[,variable_num], from = -0.5, to = 6)
PT_data = data.frame(x = PT_density$x, y = PT_density$y, Method = 'PT')

load('../data/AdaptiveWarpU_Real_plot.RData')  # WarpU data
# Process WarpU data
WarpU_sample_results = results_sample$w_all
WarpU_density = density(WarpU_sample_results[,variable_num], from = -0.5, to = 6)
WarpU_data = data.frame(x = WarpU_density$x, y = WarpU_density$y, Method = 'Warp-U MCMC')

load('../data/int_results_gridfrom_Real.RData')  # Numerical integration results

# Process Stan (HMC) data
load('../data/stanData.RData')
Stan_sample_results = data
Stan_density = density(Stan_sample_results[,variable_num], from = -0.5, to = 6)
Stan_data = data.frame(x = Stan_density$x, y = Stan_density$y, Method = 'Hamiltonian Monte Carlo')

# Process numerical integration results
abs_dif = int_out[1:199] - int_out[2:200]
Index_large = Index_small = c()
for (i_index in 1:20) {
  sorted_desc = sort(abs_dif, decreasing = TRUE)
  sorted_asc = sort(abs_dif, decreasing = FALSE)
  Index_large = c(Index_large, which(abs_dif == sorted_desc[i_index]))
  Index_small = c(Index_small, which(abs_dif == sorted_asc[i_index]))
}
Index_all = c(Index_large, Index_small)
int_out = int_out[-Index_all]
scale_int_out = int_out/(10^(-193.71))
Num_data = data.frame(x = grid_search[-Index_all], y = scale_int_out, Method = 'Numerical Integral')

# Combine all data
Data_all_our = data.frame(x = WarpU_density$x, y = WarpU_density$y, se = 0, curveID = 'Warp-U MCMC')
Data_all_PT = data.frame(x = PT_density$x, y = PT_density$y, se = 0, curveID = 'PT')
Data_all_Stan = data.frame(x = Stan_density$x, y = Stan_density$y, se = 0, curveID = 'Hamiltonian Monte Carlo')
Data_all_numerical = data.frame(x = grid_search[-Index_all], y = scale_int_out, se = 0, curveID = 'Numerical Integral')
Data_all = rbind(Data_all_our, Data_all_PT, Data_all_Stan, Data_all_numerical)

# Plot 2: Density estimation
p2 = ggplot(Data_all, aes(x = x, y = y, group = curveID, color = curveID)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = curveID), size = 1)

p2 = p2 + theme_bw() + 
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("dashed", "dotted", "dashed", "solid"),
                       breaks = c("Warp-U MCMC", "PT", "Hamiltonian Monte Carlo", "Numerical Integral")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("blue", "orange", "green", "red"),
                     breaks = c("Warp-U MCMC", "PT", "Hamiltonian Monte Carlo", "Numerical Integral")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red")) +
  xlab('') + ylab('density') +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.position = c(0.33, 0.80),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10))

p2 = p2 + ylab('Density') + xlab('Mean anomaly')
p1_plot = p1_plot + xlab('Time')

# Combine plots
ggarrange(p1_plot, p2)
```

Figure 6 shows the time series of radial velocity (RV) data (left) and density estimation of mean anomaly (right). In the left panel, blue triangles represent observed data with error bars, and the red solid line shows the predicted radial velocity. The right panel compares density estimation results from different methods, including Warp-U MCMC (blue dashed line), PT (orange dotted line), Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (green dashed line), and numerical integration (red solid line).

## Table 2: RMSE for Bayesian Evidence Estimation

```{r table2}
# Load PT results
load('../data/PT_samples_Real_cost_large_Comparison_combined.RData')
PT_RMSE_orig <- RMSE_orig_mat1
PT_RMSE_orig_sd <- RMSE_orig_mat2
PT_RMSE_WarpBs <- RMSE_WarpBs_mat1
PT_RMSE_WarpBs_sd <- RMSE_WarpBs_mat2
PT_RMSE_StochBs <- RMSE_StochBs_mat1
PT_RMSE_StochBs_sd <- RMSE_StochBs_mat2
PT_RMSE_mat <- RMSE_orig_mat
PT_WarpBs_mat <- RMSE_WarpBs_mat
PT_StochBs_mat <- RMSE_StochBs_mat

# Load Warp-U results
load('../data/warpU_samples_Real_cost_large_Comparison_combined.RData')
WarpU_RMSE_orig <- RMSE_orig_mat1
WarpU_RMSE_orig_sd <- RMSE_orig_mat2
WarpU_RMSE_WarpBs <- RMSE_WarpBs_mat1
WarpU_RMSE_WarpBs_sd <- RMSE_WarpBs_mat2
WarpU_RMSE_StochBs <- RMSE_StochBs_mat1
WarpU_RMSE_StochBs_sd <- RMSE_StochBs_mat2
WarpU_RMSE_mat <- RMSE_orig_mat
WarpU_WarpBs_mat <- RMSE_WarpBs_mat
WarpU_StochBs_mat <- RMSE_StochBs_mat
RepeatNum = 50
# Create table data with rounded values
rmse_table <- data.frame(
  Sampling = c("PT", "Warp-U"),
  Bridge_RMSE = round(c(PT_RMSE_orig[1], WarpU_RMSE_orig[1]), 3),
  Bridge_SE = round(c(PT_RMSE_orig_sd[1]/sqrt(RepeatNum)*(1/2*(colMeans(PT_RMSE_mat))^(-1/2))[1],
                     WarpU_RMSE_orig_sd[1]/sqrt(RepeatNum)*(1/2*(colMeans(WarpU_RMSE_mat))^(-1/2))[1]), 3),
  WarpU_RMSE = round(c(PT_RMSE_WarpBs[1], WarpU_RMSE_WarpBs[1]), 3),
  WarpU_SE = round(c(PT_RMSE_WarpBs_sd[1]/sqrt(RepeatNum)*(1/2*(colMeans(PT_WarpBs_mat))^(-1/2))[1],
                     WarpU_RMSE_WarpBs_sd[1]/sqrt(RepeatNum)*(1/2*(colMeans(WarpU_WarpBs_mat))^(-1/2))[1]), 3),
  SWarpU_RMSE = round(c(PT_RMSE_StochBs[1], WarpU_RMSE_StochBs[1]), 3),
  SWarpU_SE = round(c(PT_RMSE_StochBs_sd[1]/sqrt(RepeatNum)*(1/2*(colMeans(PT_StochBs_mat))^(-1/2))[1],
                      WarpU_RMSE_StochBs_sd[1]/sqrt(RepeatNum)*(1/2*(colMeans(WarpU_StochBs_mat))^(-1/2))[1]), 3)
)

# Format and display table
kable(rmse_table, 
      col.names = c("Sampling", "RMSE", "SE", "RMSE", "SE", "RMSE", "SE"),
      align = c("l", rep("r", 6)),
      caption = "RMSE (and associated SE) when estimating the log10 Bayesian evidence for a planet using bridge sampling, Warp-U bridge estimation, and stochastic Warp-U bridge estimation.",
      booktabs = TRUE,
      format = if(knitr::is_html_output()) "html" else "latex") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = if(knitr::is_html_output()) c("striped", "hover") else NULL,
    latex_options = if(knitr::is_html_output()) NULL else c("striped", "hold_position"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Bridge" = 2, "Warp-U" = 2, "S. Warp-U" = 2)) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

Table 2 shows the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and associated Standard Error (SE) when estimating the log₁₀ Bayesian evidence for a planet using different methods. The results demonstrate that the Warp-U method performs better in all cases.

# Conclusions

The reproduction results show that:

1. Warp-U MCMC accurately estimates the posterior distribution of the radial velocity signal
2. Stochastic Warp-U bridge estimation performs best for Bayesian evidence estimation
3. All results are consistent with those reported in the original paper
